import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Convert date and time to a single datetime object
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract hour of the day
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour

# Aggregate sales data by product and hour
hourly_sales = df.groupby(['product', 'hour'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Find the top 5 best-selling products to keep the plot clean
top_products = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().nlargest(5).index
hourly_sales_top5 = hourly_sales[hourly_sales['product'].isin(top_products)]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 9))

# Create the line plot
ax = sns.lineplot(
    data=hourly_sales_top5,
    x='hour',
    y='total',
    hue='product',
    style='product',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5,
    markersize=8
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set title and labels with enhanced formatting
ax.set_title(
    'Hourly Sales Performance for Top 5 Coffee Shop Products',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Customize ticks
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(2)) # Ticks every 2 hours
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.0f}'))

# Customize the legend
legend = ax.legend(title='Product', fontsize=12, title_fontsize=14, bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left')
legend.get_frame().set_alpha(0.9)
legend.get_frame().set_edgecolor('black')

# Add a grid for better readability
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Set plot limits to give some padding
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 23.5)
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)

# Final layout adjustment
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust layout to make space for legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
